blockMcqs.question: What property must a concurrent schedule satisfy to be correct?
options: It must run each transaction in parallel
It must use the fewest locks
blockMcqs.explanation: Serializability means the outcome equals some serial execution — this is the standard correctness criterion for concurrency control.

blockMcqs.question: Which anomaly causes one transaction's write to silently overwrite another's?
blockMcqs.explanation: A lost update occurs when two transactions both read a value, compute updates, and the second write erases the first.

blockMcqs.question: Which lock combination is compatible and can be held by two transactions simultaneously?
blockMcqs.explanation: Multiple transactions can hold a shared (read) lock simultaneously since reads don't conflict. Any combination involving an exclusive lock blocks.

blockMcqs.question: In 2PL, what happens after a transaction releases its first lock?
options: It may acquire more locks of any type
It can only release locks — no new acquisitions
blockMcqs.explanation: Releasing the first lock marks the start of the shrinking phase. From that point the transaction can only release, never acquire.

blockMcqs.question: Which 2PL variant eliminates deadlocks by acquiring all locks before the transaction begins?
blockMcqs.explanation: Conservative (static) 2PL pre-declares and acquires all locks upfront, so no transaction waits mid-execution and deadlocks cannot occur.

blockMcqs.question: What does timestamp ordering do when a transaction violates the timestamp order?
options: Waits for the other transaction to commit
Acquires a shared lock and retries
Rolls back and restarts with a newer timestamp
blockMcqs.explanation: Timestamp ordering has no waiting — a violating transaction is rolled back immediately and restarted with a fresh (later) timestamp.

blockMcqs.question: What is the purpose of an intention lock in multiple granularity locking?
options: To lock every row in a table at once
To signal intent to lock a descendant node
To convert a shared lock to exclusive
blockMcqs.explanation: Intention locks (IS, IX, SIX) on ancestor nodes warn other transactions that a finer-grained lock will be taken below, preventing conflicting coarse locks.

blockMcqs.question: In MVCC, what do readers access while a writer is modifying a row?
options: The row is locked; readers wait
An older version valid at their start timestamp
blockMcqs.explanation: MVCC keeps multiple row versions. Readers see the snapshot current at their transaction start, so they never wait for a writer working on a newer version.

blockMcqs.question: Which protocol never blocks but may restart a transaction when a conflict is detected?
blockMcqs.explanation: Timestamp ordering detects order violations and restarts the offending transaction immediately instead of waiting — no blocking, but potential for cascading restarts.
